# Market Segment

**Assumptions:** The company profile has no product description or named competitors. Acme Advisory's own website describes it as an AI consulting practice helping executives and their organizations lead AI transformation. I used that to define the segment. Third-party market figures are analyst estimates and vary widely. Source quality is mixed, and several sources are vendor blogs.

## Industry

- **Primary industry:** AI consulting and advisory services. This sits inside management and IT consulting.
- **Sub-sectors Acme Advisory claims (from its website):**
  - AI Transformation & Change Leadership: strategy, governance and organizational change.
  - AI Sales Enablement & Automation: AI for sales and marketing teams.
  - AI Compliance & ISO 42001: AI governance and certification support.
- **Delivery model:** Sam Rivera helps executives lead their organization's AI transformation. This is a solo, founder-led practice (profile: "Just me").
- **Adjacent categories:**
  - AI governance software and platforms. These are products, not services.
  - ISO 42001 advisory and audit services. One report says ISO 42001 certification is generating a secondary market in advisory and audit services.
- **Buyer segmentation used by analysts:** Reports split the market by enterprise size (small and mid-sized vs large enterprise). They also split it by end-user vertical. Acme Advisory's site does not name a target size or vertical. That is a positioning gap.

## Position

- **Classification:** Emerging niche player. This is my assessment, not a sourced fact.
  - It is a one-person practice, so it has no scale or market share in a market led by global firms.
  - The website does not list case studies, named clients or a team in the retrieved snippet. Not available for review beyond the snippet.
- **Where the market is led:**
  - Tier 1 strategy houses and Big Four firms dominate the large-enterprise tier. One ranking lists McKinsey QuantumBlack, BCG X and Bain Vector for strategy, and Deloitte AI, EY.ai, KPMG Lighthouse and PwC AI for Big-4 governance.
- **Where a solo practice can credibly play:**
  - Advisors suggest matching firm type to the buyer's constraint. Strategy gaps point to MBB and Big Four. Build gaps point to boutiques, dev shops or a fractional team.
  - Acme Advisory is strategy, governance and change. That puts it in the strategy lane, against the biggest brands. It needs a sharper wedge than "AI strategy for executives".
- **Possible wedges visible in its own copy:**
  - The ISO 42001 certification path.
  - AI for sales and marketing teams, including competitive intelligence.
  - The "Define Your North" and 79°N Svalbard brand idea.
  - Which wedge to lead with is a decision for the next steps.

## Size

**TAM: global AI consulting services.** Estimates differ by source and definition. No single figure is authoritative.

| Source | 2025 value | Forecast | CAGR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wiseguy Reports | $5.16B in 2025, $25B by 2035 | 2035 | about 17.1% |
| The Business Research Company | $7.39B in 2025, $19.47B by 2030 | 2030 | 21.4% |
| Fortune Business Insights | $9.65B in 2025 | $73.89B by 2034 | 25.6% |
| Future Market Insights | $11.07B in 2025, $90.99B by 2035 | 2035 | 23.4% |
| Business Research Insights | $11.13B in 2025, $116.81B by 2034 | 2034 | 26.49% |

- **Range:** roughly $5B to $11B in 2025. Growth forecasts run from about 17% to 26.5% a year. One roundup concludes the market is growing between 20 and 26% annually.
- **Region:** North America held a 38.13% share in 2025. Applied to Fortune's $9.65B, that is about $3.7B. This is my own arithmetic.

**Adjacent market: AI governance.** This is mostly software, so it is an upper bound for Acme Advisory's governance service line, not a direct TAM.
- Estimates for 2025 range from $309M (Precedence Research) to $353M (IMARC) and $940M (Next Move Strategy Consulting).
- Growth forecasts run from 28.15% a year (Mordor Intelligence, $440M in 2026 to $1.51B by 2031) to 51% a year (Next Move).
- One outlier report puts the 2025 market at $5.9B with 10.9% growth. I treat it as non-comparable because the definition is unclear.

**SAM for Acme Advisory:** Not available. No source sizes executive-level AI strategy, governance and change advisory for solo or boutique providers. The profile gives no target geography, buyer size or pricing, so I did not estimate one. To size it, define the target buyer first (for example, mid-market firms in one region). Then count the firms and multiply by an assumed engagement value.

## Competitors

**Market share data:** Not available. I found no reliable share figures by firm.

**Tier 1: strategy houses.** These win on board-level credibility.
- **McKinsey QuantumBlack:** roughly 1,700 people across 40+ offices.
- **BCG X:** about 3,000 technologists and data scientists combined with BCG's strategy consulting. It also often brings a working demo into the room with the recommendation.
- **Bain Vector:** one ranking calls it the best Tier 1 firm for private-equity-backed AI value creation.
- BCG's "10-20-70" model puts 70% of effort into people and process. This overlaps directly with Acme Advisory's change-leadership message.

**Tier 2: Big Four and global integrators.** These win on governance, controls and scale.
- Deloitte AI, PwC AI, EY.ai and KPMG Lighthouse.
- Accenture and IBM Consulting. One source says Accenture has the largest GenAI practice.
- Deloitte is positioned for governance and controls. This is the main competitor for the ISO 42001 and compliance offer.

**Tier 3: boutiques and specialists.** These are the closest peers.
- Examples named in sources: AY Automate, LeewayHertz, Kanerika, Neurons Lab, Vstorm, Addepto, Tribe AI and deepsense.ai. Most skew toward engineering and building, not executive change leadership.
- A fractional Chief AI Officer is a related model. AY Automate offers hands-on strategy with a fractional Chief AI Officer.
- **Pricing:** The only figures I found come from a vendor comparison blog and should be treated as indicative. It lists day rates of $500-700/hr for McKinsey QuantumBlack and project-based $200K-1M for boutiques. No Acme Advisory pricing was found.

**Alternatives to hiring a consultant:**
- AI governance platforms. IBM announced validation against 12 regulatory frameworks in 2025.
- Internal teams and generic training.
- ISO 42001 certification bodies.

**Named competitors in the profile:** None provided. The set above is inferred from the category. The founder should confirm which ones actually show up in deals.

## Trends

1. **AI spend is high but the value gap is wide.** This is the core of Acme Advisory's message ("Most AI rollouts fail... because the organization wasn't led through the change").
   - A WRITER survey of 2,400 people found 79% of organizations face adoption challenges and 59% invest over $1M a year.
   - The same survey says 75% of executives admit their AI strategy is "more for show".
   - WRITER sells AI software, so treat these figures as vendor data.
   - Gartner (Sept 2026, via a secondary source) reports only 22% of organizations have scaled AI across multiple business units.
   - Be careful with "X% of AI projects fail" claims. Sources measure different things. One analysis calls the failure statistic the most-cited and most-abused in enterprise AI. Cite one primary study with its definition.

2. **People and change are the bottleneck.** This supports the change-leadership positioning.
   - IBM's 2026 CEO study, as cited by a secondary source, found 83% of CEOs say AI success depends more on people's adoption than on the technology.
   - A review of 163 transformation failures found 92% were primarily organizational or operational, not technical. This is a secondary source with a small sample.

3. **Governance lags deployment.**
   - IBM's AI control-gap study (2,000 executives), as summarized by a secondary source, found 67% are held accountable for AI systems they don't fully control.
   - WRITER reports 67% of executives believe their company already suffered a data breach due to unapproved AI tools. This matches the site's line about teams "using tools you haven't reviewed".

4. **Regulation and standards are creating demand.**
   - ISO/IEC 42001 is the first international AI management system standard. Roughly 350 organizations worldwide had certified by mid-2026, per industry compilations, with no official global register. The base is small and early.
   - EU AI Act dates and penalties differ across sources. One lists Article 50 applicability on 2 August 2026. Another cites penalties of up to €35 million or 7% of global turnover for the most serious violations. Verify against the official text before using either in marketing.

5. **Market growth is driven by governance and transformation demand.** One report attributes forecast growth partly to demand for responsible AI and governance frameworks and investment in AI transformation strategies.

6. **Buyers sort providers by constraint, not brand.** Advice to buyers now says the best firm fits your stage, data and talent gap, not the biggest brand. This helps a specialist boutique if it names a specific buyer and problem.

7. **Messaging crowding.** Most competitor pages use generic "AI strategy and transformation" language. Acme Advisory's current headline, "Define Your North", is brand-led and does not state a buyer or outcome. Test this in the competitor and messaging steps.

**Gaps in this research:**
- No Acme Advisory customers, pricing or case studies were found.
- No SAM or share data was found.
- Acme Advisory's full website was only seen as a search snippet.

**Sources:** acme-advisory.example; Fortune Business Insights; Future Market Insights; The Business Research Company; Wiseguy Reports; Business Research Insights; Mordor Intelligence; IMARC; Precedence Research; Next Move Strategy Consulting; NovelVista; Dialectica; WRITER; Gartner and IBM (via secondary sources); agent.nexus; Alice Labs; AY Automate; Iternal.
